title: Five Minutes Before the Alarm
scene: You wake up just before your alarm, reach for your phone, then decide to stay in bed and listen to the rain for a moment.
sceneJa: 目覚ましの5分前に目が覚める。スマホに手を伸ばしかけたが、雨音を聞きながら静かに過ごすことにする。

chunks.ja: スマホに手を伸ばした。
メッセージを確認しかけた
まだ完全に目が覚める前に。

chunks.en: Then I thought better of it
and put the phone face down.
chunks.ja: スマホを伏せて置いた。

chunks.en: There was no point in rushing
when I still had a few minutes to spare.
chunks.ja: まだ数分の余裕があったのだから。

chunks.en: I lay there listening to the rain
chunks.ja: 横になったまま雨音を聞いていた

chunks.en: until the alarm finally went off.
chunks.ja: やがて目覚ましが鳴るまで。

chunks.en: the day didn't start with a screen.
chunks.ja: 画面を見ずに一日が始まった。

questions.question: Which is the natural meaning chunk?
questions.explanation: Think better of it means to decide not to do something after reconsidering.

questions.question: What does 'out of habit' mean?
questions.explanation: Out of habit describes an automatic action you do routinely.

questions.question: Why does the speaker put the phone down?
options: They decide not to check messages immediately.
questions.explanation: The speaker chooses a quieter start instead of automatically checking messages.

speak: In 30 seconds, describe a morning habit you almost followed but reconsidered. Use 'out of habit', 'thought better of it', and 'a few minutes to spare'.
review: New: out of habit（いつもの癖で）, think better of it（考え直してやめる）, there is no point in ...-ing（〜しても意味がない）. Review: I almost ...（〜しかけた）, a few minutes to spare（数分の余裕）. Read aloud: pause after 'Out of habit'; soften your voice in the final line.
